status: measured on exact-mask public-catalogue pseudo-holdout using mirror-bridged competition rasters; organizer provenance remains unauthenticated in this environment
hypothesis: High-magnitude geodetic strain components identify actively deforming transfer zones that may be absent from the public catalogue; adding a structural prior from DEM/magnetic/gravity and a smaller topological-persistence prior can suppress broad non-structural strain halos while preserving stable lineament anchors.

layers.structural_single_scale_prior: reuse H1 single-scale DEM-curvature + magnetic-edge + gravity-edge surfaces from scripts/build_candidate.py
layers.topological_persistence_prior: reuse H1 fused H0 persistence surface from scripts/build_candidate.py

baseline_description: Mean robust-standardized absolute second-invariant, shear-rate, and dilatation-rate fields with exact-mask pooled scoring at the same 37,654-pixel budget.

evaluation.truth: public-catalogue spatial pseudo-holdout; not expert-only hidden new-fault truth
evaluation.known_fault_mask_rule: Apply the organizer-confirmed exact provided training-fault pixel mask only; no proximity buffer.
evaluation.aggregation: Pool TP, FP, and FN across the four non-overlapping guarded quadrants before calculating one DTI.

important_limits: The current rasters were brought in through a GitHub data bridge built from user-provided Dropbox mirrors, not a fresh participant-authenticated DrivenData download in this sandbox.
The public-catalogue pseudo-holdout does not estimate private or final leaderboard performance and is especially weak for near-catalogue corrections, continuations, and splays.
The candidate score is a deterministic ranking, not a calibrated probability surface.
The topological prior is inherited from H1 and remains a peak-stability prior, not a proof of line continuity or geology.
